deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the draft of Art. (§.) 9 of Riemann's Inaugural Dissertation (1851), 'Grundlagen fuer eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veraenderlichen complexen Groesse'. The previous page sets up arc length s along a boundary and the inward normal distance p. The orientation is fixed so that dx/ds = dy/dp and dy/ds = -dx/dp. The previous article proved Green's (divergence) theorem in the form int_T (X_x + Y_y) dT = -int_{dT} (X dx/dp + Y dy/dp) ds. Theorem I: if X, Y are continuous in T and X_x + Y_y = 0, then int_{dT} (X x_p + Y y_p) ds = 0, i.e. the flux of the divergence-free field (X, Y) through the boundary vanishes.

This page:

(0) Additivity / excision. Split a surface T1 (lying over the plane A) into pieces T2 and T3. The boundary integral over dT2 equals the integral over dT1 minus the integral over dT3. Where T3 reaches dT1, the two contributions cancel, because the inner normal is the same there. Every other element of dT3 is an element of dT2 traversed with the opposite inner normal, which is where the minus sign comes from.

(II) Consequence of I and (0). The value of F(dT) = int_{dT} (X x_p + Y y_p) ds is unchanged under any enlargement or shrinking of T, provided no region is added or removed in which the hypotheses of I fail. In modern terms, the flux of a divergence-free field depends only on the homology class of the boundary in the domain of regularity.

Transition to singularities. Suppose X_x + Y_y = 0 holds everywhere except on isolated lines or points where X, Y are discontinuous. Enclose each such line or point in an arbitrarily small 'Huelle' (envelope).

(III) The flux through dT equals the sum of the fluxes through the small curves enclosing the singular sets. Each such flux is independent of how tightly the curve is drawn (by II).

Removable point singularity. Suppose that, as the distance rho to an isolated singular point goes to 0, both rho*X and rho*Y go to 0. Then the flux around that point is 0. Riemann's argument uses polar coordinates (rho, phi) centred at the point and takes as envelope the circle of radius rho. The flux is then int_0^{2pi} (X x_p + Y y_p) rho dphi; on this circle x_p = -cos phi and y_p = -sin phi (my explicitation, inward normal of the excised disk's complement). If this flux had a nonzero value K, choose rho so small that |(X x_p + Y y_p) rho| < |K|/(2pi) for all phi ('abgesehen vom Zeichen' = in absolute value). Then |integral| < |K|, a contradiction, since by III the value does not depend on rho.

(IV) Path independence. Take a simply connected surface over A in which int (X x_p + Y y_p) ds = int (Y x_s - X y_s) ds vanishes over the boundary of every subregion. (The two integrands agree by x_s = y_p, y_s = -x_p.) Then for fixed O_0 and O, int_{O_0}^{O} (Y x_s - X y_s) ds has the same value along every path in the surface. The proof begins: two paths s1 and s2 together form a closed curve s3. Either it is simple, so it bounds a subregion and the integral vanishes, or it has multiple points. That case is continued on the next folio, by decomposition into simple loops.

Modern content of IV: the 1-form X dy - Y dx is closed, hence exact on a simply connected domain. Its primitive is the stream function / harmonic conjugate. Riemann then uses this to build the conjugate function and the complex function.
errors: No mathematical errors. Minor imprecisions only.
In III the hypothesis 'rho X and rho Y become infinitely small' has to be read as uniform in phi for the choice of rho to work for all phi; Riemann implicitly assumes this.
The inequalities should be in absolute value (strictly, < |K|/(2pi) and < |K|). Riemann adds 'abgesehen vom Zeichen' in the margin, which covers this.
In (0) the cancellation statement implicitly assumes the boundaries are piecewise smooth and that T3 meets dT1 in arcs. This is standard tacit regularity for the period.
The proof of IV for non-simple closed curves is not completed on this page (it continues overleaf).

results.what: Flux of a divergence-free plane field through a boundary is invariant under deformation of the region avoiding singularities (Satz II), via excision/additivity of boundary integrals
results.modern_name: Cauchy-type integral theorem / homology invariance of integrals of closed forms (Green's theorem consequence)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Green, Cauchy (1825); in this form Riemann, Dissertation 1851

results.what: Total flux equals the sum of fluxes around isolated singularities, each independent of the enclosing curve (Satz III)
results.modern_name: Residue-type decomposition for closed 1-forms / divergence-free fields

results.what: Isolated point singularity with rho*X, rho*Y -> 0 contributes zero flux
results.modern_name: Removable-singularity-type lemma (zero residue / zero flux under o(1/r) growth)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, Dissertation 1851, Art. 9 (cf. Riemann's removable singularity theorem)

results.what: Vanishing flux over every subregion of a simply connected domain implies path independence of int (Y dx - X dy) (Satz IV)
results.modern_name: Closed forms are exact on simply connected domains; existence of stream function / harmonic conjugate

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of Art. 9 (Saetze I-IV) of Riemann's published 1851 doctoral dissertation; the content and even the wording match the printed text closely. It is well known as Riemann's and routine for a specialist.

transcription_corrections: The surface letters transcribed as S_1, S_2, S_3 and S are, in keeping with the previous page ('T_1 in zwei Stuecke T_2 und T_3'), almost certainly Riemann's T (T_1, T_2, T_3, T), as in the printed dissertation. Under that reading the first sentence reads: Begrenzung von T_2 = Differenz der Integrale ueber T_1 und T_3.

'wenn mit der Entfernung rho des Punktes O von demselben' is correct. The marginal insertions 'beschriebenen Kreis, so erhaelt man fuer diesen Werth den Ausdruck' and 'einen von Null verschiedenen Werth K haben' replace the struck text. The final reading is: 'das auf ihn bezuegliche Integral kann folglich nicht einen von Null verschiedenen Werth K haben'.
'abgesehen vom Zeichen' is inserted after 'dass', and 'fuer jeden Werth von phi' is moved above the expression (X x_p + Y y_p) rho.
In IV the second integrand is (Y dx/ds - X dy/ds); the image partly shows the denominators as ds, not dp, and the transcription's ds is correct.
